summary: Fixed a corrupted /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance script on node1 (it contained leftover heredoc artifacts instead of valid shell), made it executable, and installed a root crontab entry running it daily at 02:15 with output appended to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log. Verified the script runs and logs correctly, then performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id/service state, issued a native systemctl reboot, confirmed connection loss then recovery, proved boot_id changed (5fb1b173... -> ac5fb70b...), and confirmed crond, the cron entry, script permissions, and log data all survived the restart, with a fresh post-restart log append succeeding.
actions_performed: Inspected existing /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance and found it corrupted with leftover heredoc/chmod text
Rewrote the script to a valid POSIX sh script and set mode 0755 root:root
Ran the script manually to confirm it executes and prints expected output
Verified crond is active and enabled, and manually ran the exact cron command line to confirm log file creation and append behavior
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime -s, crond status, crontab contents, log contents
Issued an asynchronous 'systemctl reboot' on node1 so the exec call could return before disconnection
Polled node1 until it reconnected, confirming a Connection reset then successful reconnect
Confirmed boot_id changed and uptime -s advanced, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified crond active/enabled, crontab entry, script executable bit, and log file contents post-restart
Ran the script again post-restart and confirmed it appended a new line to the existing log

evidence.requirement: inventory-maintenance script exists, is executable, and runs correctly
evidence.summary: Discovered the script was corrupted (leftover heredoc text), rewrote it as valid POSIX sh, chmod 0755, and confirmed it runs producing the expected output.

evidence.requirement: Cron job scheduled daily at 02:15 running the script and appending to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
evidence.summary: Installed root crontab entry '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' and manually executed the exact cron command line, confirming the log file is created and contains the expected line.
Captured boot_id=5fb1b173..., uptime -s, crond active, crontab entry present, and existing log contents before restart.
Issued 'systemctl reboot' via a backgrounded/disowned shell so the exec call acknowledged and returned immediately, before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: Proof the node actually restarted (changed boot identity)
evidence.summary: First poll still showed old boot_id (reboot not yet executed), second poll hit connection reset (node rebooting), third poll showed boot_id changed to ac5fb70b... and a later uptime -s, proving the restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron service, job, script, and log data
evidence.summary: After reconnect, confirmed crond active/enabled, crontab entry intact, script still executable, prior log content preserved, and a fresh script run successfully appended a new log line.
